newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi second bank to list on Beirut exchange.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi second bank to list on Beirut exchange.

text.p: Banque Audi, one of Lebanon's most active banks, has won approval to list its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange -- the second commercial bank to list on the market in a little over two weeks.

"The Beirut bourse committee has accepted on January 9, 1997, the listing of Banque Audi's C shares in the bourse's official market. Trading will start as of January 20, 1997," the Beirut Stock Exchange said in a statement.

At least one other leading Beirut bank, Byblos Bank, is also expected to list its shares soon. Dealers say they expect the bank shares to invigorate the stock exchange which has been mostly lacklustre since it reopened last January.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was the first bank to list its shares on the exchange since it reopened last year after a 13-year shutdown due to Lebanon's civil war.

BLC shares have been the star performer on the market since they began trading on December 30. BLC shares, which on Wednesday were unchanged from Tuesday's $12.375, have steadily risen from their initial price of $11.25 when they began trading.
The two bank listings were allowed under a law passed last year that allows Lebanese banks to list and trade 30 percent of their shares on the exchange without prior permission from the central bank.
Audi, Byblos and BLC, are among Lebanon's most dynamic banks. All three have in the past 17 months raised capital through public or private share issues on local and international markets.
In its statement, the Beirut Stock Exchange said a price has not been set for Banque Audi's shares yet.
Ten shares of six companies are currently trading on the exchange, which has a capitalisation of $2.5 billion.
Banque Audi launched a heavily oversubscribed $100 million Eurobond in October lead-managed by Merrill Lynch International.
It is the third Lebanese bank by size of capital, which now stands at $63 million, and in 1995 was ranked third among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks in terms of customer deposits.
Audi reported profits of 14 billion Lebanese pounds ($9 million) in the first half of 1996 compared to 20 billion pounds for the whole of 1995. ($1 = 1,551 Lebanese pounds)
